1	# Task 065
2	
3	The supplied project is used to inspect fields reconstructed from particles in
4	hydrodynamic simulations. A normal analysis workflow completes on the bundled
5	workload and produces finite observations, but a reported scientific quantity
6	can change when the same particle data are used through another valid numerical
7	representation. This can affect comparisons between otherwise compatible
8	analyses rather than merely changing the appearance of a plot.
9	
10	Read the accompanying method material and the local visualization notes. Run
11	the public reproduction first, then inspect the historical source and trace the
12	ordinary public workflows that load the particle data and construct the
13	observations. Repair the implementation so that the documented scientific
14	quantity is correct and stable for supported representations of the same
15	physical input.
16	
17	The change must be a general repair to the project under `source/`. Do not
18	replace the workload, edit the public reproduction to hide the observation, or
19	hard-code its values. Use the supplied scientific definitions and the source's
20	public API to investigate the discrepancy, and validate the repair with input
21	variations of your own. Keep the public API usable and preserve valid behavior
22	outside the reported case.

1	A hydrodynamics analysis produces finite particle-field observations, but a
2	corresponding scientific value changes when the same valid particle input is
3	used through another numerical representation of the observation. The effect
4	is large enough to alter comparisons between otherwise compatible analyses.
5	
6	Using the supplied scientific material, visualization notes, source snapshot,
7	and public reproduction, identify and repair the implementation. The repair
8	must generalize to supported particle-field workflows and must not special-case
9	the bundled workload.

1	# Public reproduction
2	
3	Run from this directory after the task runtime has built the bundled source:
4	
5	```bash
6	python reproduce.py
7	```
8	
9	The command loads the deterministic particle workload through yt's public
10	particle-data interface, performs the same public projection workflow for two
11	fixed viewing configurations, and records finite summaries of corresponding
12	samples from several valid numerical representations within each configuration.
13	It writes:
14	
15	```text
16	outputs/public_reproduction_report.json
17	```
18	
19	The report contains the observations produced by these local workflows and a
20	descriptive summary. Each configuration reports the finite fraction, sample
21	count, mean, and observed range of a corresponding physical sample across its
22	representations. The two configurations are not expected to have the same
23	physical value; the relevant observation is the range within each one. These
24	are diagnostic observations, not a correctness verdict or a private acceptance
25	threshold. Human-readable floating-point summaries are rounded to remove
26	machine-roundoff noise; the underlying source workflow is not rounded before it
27	produces the observations.
28	
29	The machine-readable lifecycle states are:
30	
31	- `workflow_completed`, exit code `0`: the local scientific workflow completed
32	  and produced finite observations;
33	- `runner_failure`, exit code `2`: the source could not be imported/built, the
34	  workload could not be loaded, or the workflow did not produce a finite
35	  observation.
36	
37	`workflow_completed` means that the local scientific workflows completed and
38	produced finite observations. A `runner_failure` means that the workflows could
39	not be completed in the local task environment. A completed workflow is not
40	itself a claim that the observations are scientifically consistent; the task
41	requires the implementation to be repaired and validated more broadly.

10	`particle_position_z`. An SPH-capable particle dataset also supplies a mass,
11	density, and smoothing-length field. Values may be given as `(array, unit)`
12	pairs, and the dataset has an explicit bounding box and periodicity metadata.
13	
14	The loader creates an in-memory dataset. The particle field is still a
15	scientific field, not an image pixel value: its units and normalization must be
16	preserved by later analysis.
17	
18	## Projections and slices
19	
20	An axis-aligned projection integrates a field along a selected coordinate
21	direction and returns a two-dimensional representation. `ProjectionPlot` and
22	the data-object projection route are ordinary public ways to request this
23	operation. A fixed-resolution buffer can represent the result at a chosen
24	image size without changing the underlying simulation. When the physical
25	window and a corresponding pixel-center location are held fixed, the SPH
26	quantity at that location is the meaningful object to compare; statistics over
27	all pixels need not be identical.
28	
29	A slice evaluates a particle-reconstructed field on a plane. An off-axis view
30	uses a normal vector and an in-plane orientation to express the same type of
31	scientific observation in another coordinate frame. Different normal vectors
32	describe different physical lines of sight and must not be compared as though
33	they were the same scalar observation. For one fixed normal, however,
34	corresponding sample locations across valid numerical representations refer to
35	the same underlying field quantity.
36	
37	## Periodic domains
38	
39	For a periodic simulation, a particle near a domain face represents the same
40	physical material as its translated periodic image. Periodicity is a property
41	of the dataset and can affect which particle images are visible in a selected
42	region. A valid view should not acquire a physical excess merely because a
43	representation crosses a periodic boundary.
44	
45	## Reading the result
46	
47	The generated report is a record of finite-state information and descriptive
48	sample summaries produced by the local workflow. It intentionally does not
49	publish a correctness threshold or complete image. Interpret its
50	within-configuration sample variation together with the particle method and
51	the public API semantics; do not compare values from different viewing
52	configurations.
53	
54	## Official references

58	- yt visualization and fixed-resolution-buffer documentation:
59	  https://yt-project.org/doc/visualizing/plots.html

30	def _sample_ray(ray, npoints, field):
31	    """
32	    Private function that uses a ray object for calculating the field values
33	    that will be the y-axis values in a LinePlot object.
34	
35	    Parameters
36	    ----------
37	    ray : YTOrthoRay, YTRay, or LightRay
38	        Ray object from which to sample field values
39	    npoints : int
40	        The number of points to sample
41	    field : str or field tuple
42	        The name of the field to sample
43	    """
44	    start_point = ray.start_point
45	    end_point = ray.end_point
46	    sample_dr = (end_point - start_point) / (npoints - 1)
47	    sample_points = [np.arange(npoints) * sample_dr[i] for i in range(3)]
48	    sample_points = uvstack(sample_points).T + start_point
49	    ray_coordinates = uvstack([ray["index", d] for d in "xyz"]).T
50	    ray_dds = uvstack([ray["index", f"d{d}"] for d in "xyz"]).T
51	    ray_field = ray[field]
52	    field_values = ray.ds.arr(np.zeros(npoints), ray_field.units)
53	    for i, sample_point in enumerate(sample_points):
54	        ray_contains = (sample_point >= (ray_coordinates - ray_dds / 2)) & (
55	            sample_point <= (ray_coordinates + ray_dds / 2)
56	        )
57	        ray_contains = ray_contains.all(axis=-1)
58	        # use argmax to find the first nonzero index, sometimes there
59	        # are two indices if the sampling point happens to fall exactly at
60	        # a cell boundary
61	        field_values[i] = ray_field[np.argmax(ray_contains)]
62	    dr = np.sqrt((sample_dr**2).sum())
63	    x = np.arange(npoints) / (npoints - 1) * (dr * npoints)
64	    return x, field_values

    yc = y_min + (np.arange(N)+0.5)*dy

import sys

import numpy as np
import yt
from yt.utilities.lib.pixelization_routines import SPHKernelInterpolationTable

FAIL = []


def check(name, cond, info=""):
    status = "PASS" if cond else "FAIL"
    if not cond:
        FAIL.append(name)
    print(f"[{status}] {name} {info}")


def make_ds(seed=1, shape=(7, 7, 7), hsml=0.12, jitter=0.10, bbox=((0., 0., 0.), (3., 3., 3.)),
            central_mult=1.8, kernel_name="cubic", periodicity=(True, True, True)):
    shape = tuple(shape)
    left = np.asarray(bbox[0], dtype=np.float64)
    right = np.asarray(bbox[1], dtype=np.float64)
    spacing = (right - left) / np.asarray(shape, dtype=np.float64)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    positions = []
    for i in range(shape[0]):
        for j in range(shape[1]):
            for k in range(shape[2]):
                index = np.asarray((i, j, k), dtype=np.float64)
                point = left + (index + 0.5) * spacing
                if (i, j, k) != tuple(value // 2 for value in shape):
                    point = point + rng.uniform(-1.0, 1.0, 3) * spacing * jitter
                positions.append(point)
    positions = np.asarray(positions)
    centered = positions - 0.5 * (left + right)
    normalized = centered / (right - left)
    masses = 1.0 + 0.12 * np.sin(5.0 * normalized[:, 0]) ** 2
    masses[len(masses) // 2] *= central_mult
    density = 2.0 * masses
    field = (1.0 + 0.25 * normalized[:, 0] + 0.18 * normalized[:, 1] ** 2
             + 0.10 * np.cos(3.0 * normalized[:, 2]))
    smoothing = np.full(len(masses), hsml)
    data = {
        "particle_position_x": (positions[:, 0], "cm"),
        "particle_position_y": (positions[:, 1], "cm"),
        "particle_position_z": (positions[:, 2], "cm"),
        "particle_mass": (masses / 729.0, "g"),
        "density": (density, "g/cm**3"),
        "smoothing_length": (smoothing, "cm"),
        "tracer": (field, "erg/g"),
    }
    ds = yt.load_particles(data, length_unit=1.0,
                           bbox=np.asarray(bbox, dtype=float).T,
                           periodicity=periodicity)
    ds.kernel_name = kernel_name
    aux = dict(positions=positions, masses=masses / 729.0, density=density,
               field=field, hsml=hsml, box=right - left)
    return ds, aux


def analytic_axis(ds, aux, xp, yp, ax):
    """SPLASH column quantity at in-plane point (xp,yp): sum m f/rho g(q)/h^2."""
    oax = [a for a in range(3) if a != ax]
    pos = aux["positions"]
    box = aux["box"]
    itab = SPHKernelInterpolationTable(ds.kernel_name)
    tot = 0.0
    for i in range(pos.shape[0]):
        d0 = abs(pos[i, oax[0]] - xp)
        d1 = abs(pos[i, oax[1]] - yp)
        if ds.periodicity[oax[0]]:
            d0 = min(d0, box[oax[0]] - d0)
        if ds.periodicity[oax[1]]:
            d1 = min(d1, box[oax[1]] - d1)
        r2 = d0 * d0 + d1 * d1
        h = aux["hsml"]
        if r2 >= h * h:
            continue
        g = itab.interpolate_array(np.array([r2 / (h * h)]))[0]
        tot += aux["masses"][i] * aux["field"][i] / aux["density"][i] * g / (h * h)
    return tot


def sample_center(ds, normal, N, width=3.0, north=None):
    kw = {}
    if not isinstance(normal, (int, np.integer)):
        kw["north_vector"] = np.asarray((0.0, 1.0, 0.0)) if north is None else north
    plot = yt.ProjectionPlot(ds, normal, ("io", "tracer"), width=(width, "cm"),
                             center=ds.domain_center, buff_size=(N, N), **kw)
    img = np.asarray(plot.frb[("io", "tracer")].to_value(), dtype=np.float64)
    return img[N // 2, N // 2], img


print("== 1. Center-sample stability across grid sizes (axis-aligned) ==")
for kernel in ("cubic", "quartic", "quintic"):
    ds, aux = make_ds(kernel_name=kernel)
    truth = analytic_axis(ds, aux, 1.5, 1.5, 2)
    vals = []
    for N in (5, 9, 17, 33, 65):
        c, _ = sample_center(ds, 2, N)
        vals.append(c)
    rngo = max(vals) - min(vals)
    check(f"kernel={kernel} grid-stable center", rngo < 1e-9 * max(1.0, abs(truth)),
          f"range={rngo:.3e} vals={[f'{v:.6f}' for v in vals]}")
    check(f"kernel={kernel} center matches SPLASH analytic {truth:.8f}",
          abs(vals[-1] - truth) < 1e-9 * max(1.0, abs(truth)),
          f"N=65 value={vals[-1]:.8f}")

print("== 2. All three axes ==")
ds, aux = make_ds()
for ax in (0, 1, 2):
    truth = analytic_axis(ds, aux, 1.5, 1.5, ax)
    vals = [sample_center(ds, ax, N)[0] for N in (9, 33, 65)]
    check(f"axis={ax} stable+analytic",
          max(vals) - min(vals) < 1e-9 and abs(vals[-1] - truth) < 1e-9 * abs(truth),
          f"truth={truth:.8f} vals={vals}")

print("== 3. Off-axis config, grid stability across sizes ==")

# off-axis along a coordinate axis must equal the axis-aligned projection exactly

c_ax, _ = sample_center(ds, 2, 33)
check("off-axis (0,0,1) == axis2", abs(c_off - c_ax) < 1e-12, f"{c_off:.10f} vs {c_ax:.10f}")

print("== 4. Other pixel-center locations stable too ==")
for N in (5, 9, 17, 33):
    plot = yt.ProjectionPlot(ds, 2, ("io", "tracer"), width=(3.0, "cm"),
                             center=ds.domain_center, buff_size=(N, N))

dl = {}
for N in (5, 9, 17, 33):
    plot = yt.ProjectionPlot(ds, 2, ("io", "tracer"), width=(3.0, "cm"),
                             center=ds.domain_center, buff_size=(N, N))
    dl[N] = np.asarray(plot.frb[("io", "tracer")].to_value())
# check the finite values are stable in a couple of off-center pixels
ok = True
for i, j in ((1, 1), (0, 3), (4, 2)):
    row = [dl[N][i, j] for N in (5, 9, 17, 33)]
    if np.isfinite(row).all() and (max(row) - min(row)) > 1e-9 * max(1.0, max(map(abs, row))):
        ok = False
        print("   offcenter variation", i, j, row)
check("off-center pixel samples stable", ok)

print("== 5. Input variations: different h / jitter / lattice / multis ==")
for hsml, jit, shp, cmult in ((0.05, 0.0, (6, 6, 6), 1.0), (0.2, 0.2, (8, 8, 8), 3.0),
                              (0.12, 0.1, (7, 7, 7), 1.8), (0.3, 0.05, (5, 5, 5), 1.0)):
    ds2, aux2 = make_ds(seed=42, shape=shp, hsml=hsml, jitter=jit, central_mult=cmult)

wp = yt.ProjectionPlot(ds, 2, ("io", "tracer"), width=(3.0, "cm"),
                       center=ds.domain_center, buff_size=(17, 17), weight_field=("io", "density"))

check("weighted projection finite", np.isfinite(imw[imw != 0]).all(),

check("weighted off-axis projection finite", np.isfinite(imo[imo != 0]).all())

check("slice finite", np.isfinite(ims[ims != 0]).all(), f"center={ims[8,8]:.6f}")

                       center=ds.domain_center, buff_size=(9, 9))

import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "/workspace/task/source")
import numpy as np
import yt
from yt.utilities.lib.pixelization_routines import SPHKernelInterpolationTable

FAIL = []


def check(name, cond, info=""):
    status = "PASS" if cond else "FAIL"
    if not cond:
        FAIL.append(name)
    print(f"[{status}] {name} {info}")


def make_ds(seed=1, shape=(7, 7, 7), hsml=0.12, jitter=0.10,
            bbox=((0., 0., 0.), (3., 3., 3.)), central_mult=1.8,
            periodicity=(True, True, True)):
    shape = tuple(shape)
    left = np.asarray(bbox[0]); right = np.asarray(bbox[1])
    spacing = (right - left) / np.asarray(shape, dtype=float)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    positions = []
    for i in range(shape[0]):
        for j in range(shape[1]):
            for k in range(shape[2]):
                pt = left + (np.asarray((i, j, k), dtype=float) + 0.5) * spacing
                if (i, j, k) != tuple(v // 2 for v in shape):
                    pt = pt + rng.uniform(-1.0, 1.0, 3) * spacing * jitter
                positions.append(pt)
    positions = np.asarray(positions)
    normalized = (positions - 0.5 * (left + right)) / (right - left)
    masses = 1.0 + 0.12 * np.sin(5.0 * normalized[:, 0]) ** 2
    masses[len(masses) // 2] *= central_mult
    density = 2.0 * masses
    field = 1.0 + 0.25 * normalized[:, 0] + 0.18 * normalized[:, 1] ** 2 + 0.10 * np.cos(3.0 * normalized[:, 2])
    data = {"particle_position_x": (positions[:, 0], "cm"), "particle_position_y": (positions[:, 1], "cm"),
            "particle_position_z": (positions[:, 2], "cm"), "particle_mass": (masses / 729.0, "g"),
            "density": (density, "g/cm**3"), "smoothing_length": (np.full(len(masses), hsml), "cm"),
            "tracer": (field, "erg/g")}
    ds = yt.load_particles(data, length_unit=1.0, bbox=np.asarray(bbox, dtype=float).T,
                           periodicity=periodicity)
    ds.kernel_name = "cubic"
    return ds, dict(positions=positions, masses=masses / 729.0, density=density,
                    field=field, hsml=hsml, box=right - left, left=left)


def analytic_axis(ds, aux, xp, yp, ax):
    oax = [a for a in range(3) if a != ax]
    pos = aux["positions"]; box = aux["box"]
    itab = SPHKernelInterpolationTable("cubic")
    tot = 0.0
    for i in range(pos.shape[0]):
        d0 = abs(pos[i, oax[0]] - xp); d1 = abs(pos[i, oax[1]] - yp)
        if ds.periodicity[oax[0]]:
            d0 = min(d0, box[oax[0]] - d0)
        if ds.periodicity[oax[1]]:
            d1 = min(d1, box[oax[1]] - d1)
        r2 = d0 * d0 + d1 * d1
        h = aux["hsml"]
        if r2 >= h * h:
            continue
        g = itab.interpolate_array(np.array([r2 / (h * h)]))[0]
        tot += aux["masses"][i] * aux["field"][i] / aux["density"][i] * g / (h * h)
    return tot


print("== 4b. Same physical locations across sizes (off-center) ==")
ds, aux = make_ds()
locs = [(0.83, 0.71), (2.31, 1.17), (0.45, 2.6), (1.83, 1.23)]
for xp, yp in locs:
    truth = analytic_axis(ds, aux, xp, yp, 2)
    vals = []
    for N in (5, 9, 17, 33, 65):
        plot = yt.ProjectionPlot(ds, 2, ("io", "tracer"), width=(3.0, "cm"),
                                 center=ds.domain_center, buff_size=(N, N))
        img = np.asarray(plot.frb[("io", "tracer")].to_value())
        # pixel whose center is closest to the fixed physical location
        dx = 3.0 / N
        xi = int(np.clip((xp - 0.0) / dx - 0.5, 0, N - 1))
        yi = int(np.clip((yp - 0.0) / dx - 0.5, 0, N - 1))
        vals.append((img[yi, xi], (xp - (xi + 0.5) * dx), (yp - (yi + 0.5) * dx)))
    # when the pixel center offset (in kernel units) is similar, values must agree;
    # exact agreement only when location == pixel center for all sizes
    sim = [v[0] for v, ox, oy in vals]
    print(f"   loc=({xp:.3f},{yp:.3f}) analytic={truth:.8f} vals={[f'{v:.6f}' for v,_,_ in vals]} offs={[f'{o:.3f}/{p:.3f}' for _,o,p in vals]}")

print("== 5b. Non-periodic dataset grid stability ==")
dsn, auxn = make_ds(periodicity=(False, False, False))
for ax in (0, 2):
    truth = analytic_axis(dsn, auxn, 1.5, 1.5, ax)
    vals = []
    for N in (7, 11, 21, 43):
        plot = yt.ProjectionPlot(dsn, ax, ("io", "tracer"), width=(3.0, "cm"),
                                 center=dsn.domain_center, buff_size=(N, N))
        img = np.asarray(plot.frb[("io", "tracer")].to_value())
        vals.append(img[N // 2, N // 2])
    check(f"nonperiodic axis={ax} stable+analytic",
          max(vals) - min(vals) < 1e-9 and abs(vals[-1] - truth) < 1e-9 * abs(truth),
          f"truth={truth:.8f} vals={[f'{v:.8f}' for v in vals]}")

print("== 5c. Sparse/very small h (h=0.01), tiny lattice ==")
dss, auxs = make_ds(seed=5, shape=(4, 4, 4), hsml=0.01, jitter=0.3, central_mult=1.0)
truth = analytic_axis(dss, auxs, 1.5, 1.5, 2)
vals = []
for N in (7, 15, 31):
    plot = yt.ProjectionPlot(dss, 2, ("io", "tracer"), width=(3.0, "cm"),
                             center=dss.domain_center, buff_size=(N, N))
    img = np.asarray(plot.frb[("io", "tracer")].to_value())
    vals.append(img[N // 2, N // 2])
check("small h stable+analytic", max(vals) - min(vals) < 1e-9 * max(1, abs(truth)) and abs(vals[-1] - truth) < 1e-9 * max(1, abs(truth)),
      f"truth={truth:.6f} vals={[f'{v:.6f}' for v in vals]}")

print("== 5d. Overlapping-K regime: dense particles, large h ==")
dsd, auxd = make_ds(seed=9, shape=(9, 9, 9), hsml=0.6, jitter=0.05, central_mult=1.2)
truth = analytic_axis(dsd, auxd, 1.5, 1.5, 2)
vals = []
for N in (5, 9, 17, 33):
    plot = yt.ProjectionPlot(dsd, 2, ("io", "tracer"), width=(3.0, "cm"),
                             center=dsd.domain_center, buff_size=(N, N))
    img = np.asarray(plot.frb[("io", "tracer")].to_value())
    vals.append(img[N // 2, N // 2])
check("large h stable+analytic", max(vals) - min(vals) < 1e-9 * max(1, abs(truth)) and abs(vals[-1] - truth) < 1e-9 * abs(truth),
      f"truth={truth:.8f} vals={[f'{v:.8f}' for v in vals]}")
# In this regime the Riemann sum should converge onto the particle total
tots = []
for N in (17, 33, 65):
    plot = yt.ProjectionPlot(dsd, 2, ("io", "tracer"), width=(3.0, "cm"),
                             center=dsd.domain_center, buff_size=(N, N))
    img = np.asarray(plot.frb[("io", "tracer")].to_value())
    tots.append(np.nansum(img) * (3.0 / N) ** 2)
total_truth = float(np.sum(auxd["masses"] * auxd["field"] / auxd["density"]))
print(f"   totals conv: {tots} -> truth {total_truth:.8f}")
check("large-h totals converge to particle total", abs(tots[-1] - total_truth) < 0.02 * total_truth, "")

print("== 5e. Projection over a sub-region data_source ==")

events.text:
Done. The repair is a single, general change in the shared SPH projection kernel.

## Diagnosis

`reproduce.py` projects the SPH tracer field through yt's public `ProjectionPlot` for two fixed views at several `buff_size` values and samples the pixel sitting at the fixed physical center. Both configs (axis-aligned and off-axis) funnel into `pixelize_sph_kernel_projection` in `source/yt/utilities/lib/pixelization_routines.pyx` (the off-axis path via `off_axis_projection_SPH` → `rotate_particle_coord` → the same routine).

The scientific quantity implemented there is the SPLASH (Price 2007) column rendering: at an image-plane point, `I = Σ m·f/ρ · g(q)/h²`, with `g` the line-of-sight-integrated kernel (SPLASH eq. 30–32) and `q = r/h` the distance in kernel units. The defect enlarged the *kernel* scale to the image pixel scale (`h_j2 = fmax(hsml², dx·dy)`) while keeping the prefactor on the true smoothing length (`.../hsml[j]**2`), mixing two different length scales in one summation. As resolution changed, neither the point sample nor the deposited total stayed constant: coarse grids over-deposited by a factor `dx·dy/h²` (25× at 5×5 here), which is exactly the reported instability. In the fine-grid regime the floor stops binding and the code was already SPLASH-exact — I verified the sampled value matched my independent numpy evaluation of the SPLASH formula to 10 digits (0.48845473578…). That confirms which quantity the fine regime computes and what the coarse regimes must also produce.

## Repair

`source/yt/utilities/lib/pixelization_routines.pyx:1222` — drop the pixel-scale floor in the projection only:

```python
h_j2 = hsml[j]*hsml[j]
```

The projected SPLASH quantity is a well-defined point value (the integrated kernel `g(q)` is bounded, unlike `W/h³`), so the pixel grid no longer enters the physics. The slice (`pixelize_sph_kernel_slice`) and arbitrary-grid routines keep their floors — there the bare `W(0)/h³` genuinely needs the guard (SPLASH eq. 13), and they are outside the reported case.

## Validation

- `reproduce.py`: `observed_range` went from 0.258 → 0.0 (config a) and 0.511 → 0.0 (config b); the mean equals the analytic SPLASH value.
- Own NumPy evaluator of the SPLASH formula agrees to 10+ digits with the plotted center sample for: all three axes; periodic and non-periodic datasets; h = 0.01–0.6; varied lattices, jitters, central-mass multipliers; off-axis normals with different `north_vector`; narrow windows; non-square buffers. Samples are now grid-independent everywhere.
- Weighted projections (both paths), slices, and sub-region `data_source` projections still work and are finite; periodic vs non-periodic produce physically consistent results with no boundary excess.
- yt's own runnable tests in the area pass (17 passed, 3 skipped for missing scipy); the single failure (`test_field_cut_off_axis_octree`) was verified present on the unmodified baseline and is unrelated (grid/octree path).

The tracked built artifacts under `source/` are also refreshed from a rebuild, so both the source and the in-place extensions carry the fix; the workload, `reproduce.py`, and the public API are unchanged.
